 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN  BENCH AT JAIPUR  D.B. Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No. 258/2024 Mukesh Son Of Moolchand, Aged About 36 Years, R/o Gudha Ashiqpura, Tehsil Baswa, District-Dausa (Rajasthan)
 ----Appellant  Versus Asha W/o Mukesh D/o Chhotelal, Aged About 27 Years, R/o Near Paylet Stadium, Devnagar, Dausa, District Dausa (Ghatda Wale.)
 ----Respondent For Appellant(s) : Mr.Umesh Vyas For Respondent(s) :
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PANKAJ BHANDARI HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRAVEER BHATNAGAR Order 12/09/2024 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN  BENCH AT JAIPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant has preferred this appeal aggrieved by the order dated 18th November, 2023 passed by the Additional District Judge No.1, Bandikui, District Dausa, whereby the application, filed by the appellant under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (for short "the Act of 1955") for restitution of conjugal right, was dismissed.

entities.text: Additional District Judge No.1, Bandikui, District Dausa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. It is contended by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant wishes to keep his wife but she is not willing to stay with him and the Court below has wrongly held that the appellant has never made any efforts to win her heart.

3. We have considered the contentions and perused the impugned order dated 18th November,
2023.

4. From perusal of the impugned order, it is revealed that the application under Section 9 of the Act of 1955 was filed on 09 th [2024:RJ-JP:38820-DB] (2 of 2) [CMA-258/2024] September, 2021 and a year prior to that, an FIR bearing No.138/2020 was lodged against the appellant under Sections 498A & 406 IPC on 11th September, 2020, in which, charge sheet has been filed against the appellant.
Mukesh Son Of Moolchand vs Asha W/O Mukesh D/O Chhotelal ... on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37317396/
1 5.

entities.text: Mukesh Son Of Moolchand vs Asha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The impugned order also reveals that an application under Section 13 of the Act of 1955 has also been filed by the respondent-wife.
Mere fact that allegations of demand of dowry, criminal breach of trust and of causing cruelty & beating wife itself points out that wife has sufficient cause to stay apart from the husband.
The appellant has not made out any ground that the respondent-wife is living apart from him without any reasonable cause.
6. In view of the above, we do not find any error in the impugned order so as to issue notices.
7. Accordingly, the present appeal is dismissed at the stage of admission.

(PRAVEER BHATNAGAR),J (PANKAJ BHANDARI),J Preeti Asopa /14 Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
